Before you start, have these ready

OPERATING MODEL

Stop collecting client data manually

Turn Google Forms + Drive + Sheets + Gmail into one repeatable intake-to-dashboard loop, so every client request becomes a structured record instead of a chat message.

Client request
Google Form
Drive folder
Sheet tracker
Dashboard

Set it up in your office

  1. Create one shared Drive for the firm (Drive → New → Shared drive). Add top-level folders: Clients, Compliance, Templates, MIS. Everything in this guide lives here.
  2. Build one intake Google Form for your first workflow (Forms → Blank). Add only the fields you truly need, and mark the critical ones Required.
  3. In the Form, open the Responses tab → the green Sheets icon → Link to Sheets → create a new spreadsheet. Now every submission lands as a row automatically.
  4. In that linked Sheet, add four control columns to the right of the form data: Owner, Due date, Status, Evidence link. These four columns turn a response into accountable work.
  5. Submit one dummy entry yourself and confirm a row appears. This is your loop — you will reuse it for every use case that follows.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Every request becomes a structured record, not a chat message.
  • Documents land in the correct client / period folder from day one.
  • Partners see exceptions and ageing, not scattered follow-ups.
PILOT TARGET 50–70% manual follow-ups targeted in the pilot
FormsDriveSheets
CONTROL POINT

Every submission becomes a structured row with owner, due date, status and evidence link.

Start with the one data-collection process that creates the most daily friction.

WORKFLOW STACK

One workflow backbone, many use cases

Build the operating layer once, then reuse the same six-step spine for onboarding, document collection, compliance, CRM, query tracking and MIS.

Capture
Store
Track
Trigger
Report

Set it up in your office

  1. Adopt one spine for every workflow: Capture (Form) → Store (Drive folder rule) → Track (Sheet status) → Trigger (Gmail / Calendar reminder) → Report (dashboard). Plus a sixth rule: a named review owner for each record.
  2. Fix a folder-path standard now and never change it: Clients / Client Name / FY 2025-26 / Area. Consistent paths are what remove file-finding and version friction later.
  3. Agree one status vocabulary the whole firm uses: Requested · Received · Under review · Clarification · Closed. Put it in a hidden Lists tab and apply it with Data → Data validation.
  4. Make a few fields mandatory at capture (PAN, GSTIN, period, client) so incomplete submissions are stopped at the source instead of chased later.
  5. Save a blank Form + Sheet pair as your Template in the Templates folder. For each new use case you simply make a copy — the backbone is already built.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Mandatory fields reduce incomplete submissions at source.
  • Folder rules remove file-finding and version-control friction.
  • Status columns create live accountability for staff and partners.
PILOT TARGET 6-step reusable spine across all use cases
FormsDriveSheetsGmailCalendar
CONTROL POINT

Use mandatory fields, standard folder paths, status logic and review ownership.

The same backbone supports GST, Income Tax, audit, MCA and advisory data asks.

USE CASE 01 · CLIENT ONBOARDING

Client onboarding & KYC in one form

Replace long email checklists with one smart intake form that creates the client record, the Drive folder and the partner review task in a single pass.

Client form
Client ID
Drive folder
Partner review
Welcome mail

Set it up in your office

  1. Copy your backbone template and rename it New Client Onboarding & KYC. Add fields: PAN, GSTIN, entity / constitution, registered address, bank details, signatory, contact name, email, phone, and services required.
  2. Make PAN, GSTIN, email and phone Required. Use Forms → question menu → Response validation to enforce a PAN pattern ([A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]) and a valid email, so bad data never enters.
  3. In the linked Sheet add a Client ID column with a formula such as =UPPER(LEFT(B2,3))&TEXT(ROW()-1,"000") to mint a stable code for every new client automatically.
  4. Create the client folder set under Clients/: one parent folder named ClientID – Name with subfolders KYC, GST, Income Tax, Audit, Correspondence. (Optional: an Apps Script can create these on submit; a one-line manual SOP works perfectly to start.)
  5. Add a Partner review status column. The partner confirms all KYC fields are complete before the file is assigned, so missing data is caught up front, not mid-engagement.
  6. Send a Welcome email from a saved Gmail template (Settings → Templates) containing the document upload link and the engagement contact. Reuse the same intake form for every new client.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Basic master data is standardised across all new clients.
  • Missing fields are visible before the assignment starts.
  • The same intake form is reused for every onboarding file.
PILOT TARGET 2–4 hrs target saving per new client file
FormsDriveSheetsGmail
CONTROL POINT

PAN, GSTIN, entity, bank and contact fields are captured once and reviewed before work starts.

Useful for new GST, Income Tax, audit and retainer clients alike.

USE CASE 02 · DOCUMENT COLLECTION

Stop chasing documents on WhatsApp

Move clients from ad-hoc uploads to one Drive link with a checklist-backed status and automatic reminders, so missing files surface on their own.

Request list
Upload link
File naming
Status update
Reminder

Set it up in your office

  1. For each engagement, create one Drive folder under the client / period path and generate a single share or upload link. That one link replaces every scattered chat and email thread.
  2. Build a request checklist in Sheets — one row per required document (e.g. bank statements, sales register, purchase register, TDS certificates) with columns Document, Owner, Due date, Status, Evidence link.
  3. Publish a naming convention and put it at the top of the folder: Client_FY_DocType_v1. Consistent names kill duplicate review and version confusion.
  4. Use Conditional formatting on the Status column (red = Pending, amber = Received, green = Verified) so the gaps are visible at a glance — missing files surface automatically.
  5. Set reminders for overdue rows. Easiest start: a saved Gmail template sent on a schedule. Stronger: a mail-merge add-on or a short Apps Script that emails only the rows still marked Pending.

Why it cuts collection time

  • One upload route replaces multiple chat and email threads.
  • Missing files surface automatically for follow-up.
  • Version control reduces rework and duplicate review.
PILOT TARGET 1 link per engagement, tied to the tracker
DriveSheetsGmail
CONTROL POINT

Create one controlled folder per client / period and track missing documents from the sheet.

Best first pilot: ITR, GST reconciliation, audit PBC and notice responses.

USE CASE 03 · COMPLIANCE CONTROL

Control compliance due dates in one view

Convert scattered compliance lists into a live tracker with Calendar reminders and escalation rules, so deadlines move out of memory and diaries.

Register
Owner
Calendar
Alert
Dashboard

Set it up in your office

  1. Build a Compliance Register in Sheets with columns: Client, Obligation (GST, TDS, Advance tax, MCA, Notices), Period, Due date, Owner, Status.
  2. Give every obligation a named Owner. An obligation without an owner is the single most common reason deadlines slip.
  3. Push due dates into Google Calendar with a shared firm calendar. Set event notifications at T-7, T-3 and T-1 days so the reminder rhythm replaces last-day phone chasing.
  4. Add an ageing / escalation rule: a helper column =TODAY()-DueDate flags overdue items; anything overdue auto-rolls up to the partner view instead of relying on a phone call.
  5. Create three filtered views from the same sheet: a partner dashboard (everything by ageing), a staff worklist (only my open items) and a client exception view (what each client still owes).

Why it cuts collection time

  • T-7 / T-3 / T-1 reminders reduce last-day chasing.
  • Open items are visible by client, staff and due date.
  • Escalation is based on ageing, not phone calls.
PILOT TARGET T-7 / T-3 / T-1 reminder rhythm before every deadline
SheetsCalendar
CONTROL POINT

GST, TDS, advance tax, MCA and notice dates are tracked with owner, status and escalation.

Keep partner, staff and client views separate so each role sees only what it needs.

USE CASE 04 · CLIENT CRM

A lightweight CRM CA teams will actually use

Capture leads, next actions and conversion status without implementing a heavy CRM — a minimal pipeline stays live because it asks only for what partners need.

Lead form
Meeting note
Quote
Follow-up
Status

Set it up in your office

  1. Build a short Lead form: source (seminar / referral / website / event), contact name, firm, service interest, and notes. Share the link so any team member can log a lead in 30 seconds.
  2. Keep the pipeline Sheet to exactly five working fields: Source, Owner, Next action, Follow-up date, Stage. Resist adding more — narrowness is why it stays used.
  3. Set Stage as a validated dropdown: New · Contacted · Quoted · Won · Lost. Every prospect must have an owner and a next action at all times.
  4. Drop each follow-up date into Calendar so warm leads from seminars, referrals and events are never lost after the first conversation.
  5. Partners review the pipeline directly in the Sheet — no separate update meeting. Sort by Follow-up date to see what is due today.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Every prospect has an owner and a next action.
  • Warm leads are not lost after seminars, referrals or events.
  • Partners review the pipeline without separate update meetings.
PILOT TARGET 5 fields keep the pipeline clean and usable
FormsSheetsCalendar
CONTROL POINT

Each prospect must have source, owner, next action, follow-up date and current stage.

Keep the CRM narrow: source, owner, next action, date and stage — nothing more.

USE CASE 05 · QUERY TRACKING

Track every query until closure

Use one tracker for assessment notices, GST queries, audit PBC lists and certification requests, so each query becomes an accountable work item with ageing and evidence links.

Query raised
Owner
Response
Evidence link
Closure

Set it up in your office

  1. Create one Query Tracker Sheet that serves scrutiny notices, GST queries, audit PBC, certificates and client clarifications — one shared register instead of five scattered lists.
  2. Use columns: Query, Client, Owner, Requested data, Raised on, Due date, Response status, Evidence link, Closure remarks.
  3. Add an Ageing column =TODAY()-RaisedOn and colour it by conditional formatting. Ageing instantly shows who has not responded and where escalation is needed.
  4. Paste a Drive evidence link on the exact query row so every attachment stays tied to its query — no hunting through email for the right file.
  5. Close only when the row is complete (response + evidence + remarks). A complete record makes closure review fast and audit-ready.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Ageing shows who has not responded and where to escalate.
  • Attachments stay linked to the exact query.
  • Closure review is faster because the record is complete.
PILOT TARGET Ageing first clear overdue data before routine chasing
SheetsDriveGmail
CONTROL POINT

Assign owner, requested data, due date, response status, evidence link and closure remarks.

Useful for scrutiny, GST notices, audit PBC, certificates and client clarifications.

USE CASE 06 · PRACTICE MIS

Run your practice from live MIS

Let Sheets and Looker Studio show the state of data collection across clients, teams and periods — trackers feed a partner dashboard and generate the team's action list.

Trackers
Data model
Dashboard
Review
Action list

Set it up in your office

  1. Make sure every tracker uses the same status taxonomy from the backbone. A single status language is what lets all use cases roll up into one partner view.
  2. Build a data-model tab in one master Sheet that pulls from each tracker with IMPORTRANGE + QUERY, so all engagements collapse into one consistent table.
  3. Connect Looker Studio (free) to that master Sheet and build a partner dashboard: pending documents by client / staff / assignment, response delays by engagement type, and WIP & collection blockers side by side.
  4. Set the dashboard to refresh daily rather than producing a weekly manual MIS. The data updates itself as trackers change.
  5. End each review by exporting the open exceptions into a short action list for the team — the dashboard tells you what to do next, not just what happened.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Pending documents are visible by client, staff and assignment.
  • Response delays can be compared across engagement types.
  • Work-in-progress and collection blockers are reviewed together.
PILOT TARGET Daily refresh instead of a weekly manual MIS
SheetsLooker Studio
CONTROL POINT

Use a standard status taxonomy so all use cases roll up into one partner view.

One status language: Requested, Received, Under review, Clarification, Closed.

USE CASE 07 · KNOWLEDGE OPS

Build an internal second brain

Convert formats, replies, SOPs and case notes into searchable firm knowledge, so repeated drafting and repeated data collection shrink over time.

SOPs
Templates
Case notes
Drive index
Reuse

Set it up in your office

  1. Create a Templates / Knowledge folder holding your SOPs, standard email replies, evidence checklists and case notes in Docs — one home for everything the firm reuses.
  2. Maintain a Drive index Sheet (name, type, link, owner, last updated) so junior staff find the latest format without asking a senior.
  3. Map every repeated request to a template, SOP, evidence checklist or standard response. If a question comes up twice, it gets a reusable answer.
  4. Build a small library of standard response packs for recurring client queries so replies are consistent and fast.
  5. Make naming, versioning and owner review part of every SOP. This is what lets knowledge survive staff movement and handovers.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Junior staff find the latest format without asking seniors.
  • Repeat client queries use ready standard response packs.
  • Knowledge survives staff movement and handovers.
PILOT TARGET Reusable templates and response playbooks
DriveDocsSearch

IMPLEMENT · 7-DAY BUILD PLAN

Build the pilot in 7 working days

Start with one high-friction workflow, prove the time saved, then replicate it across use cases. Recommended first pilot: document collection or client onboarding.

Map fields
Build form
Drive rules
Tracker
Automate

Set it up in your office

  1. Day 1–2 — Map & structure. Pick one workflow, list its required fields, build the Form, and create the standard folder structure under Clients/.
  2. Day 3–5 — Track & remind. Build the linked tracker with owner / due / status / evidence, add conditional formatting and reminders, and create the partner / staff / exception views.
  3. Day 6–7 — Pilot & freeze. Run it with one client group, measure how many manual follow-ups were removed against your baseline, then freeze the SOP.
  4. Measure the baseline first. Count today's follow-ups for that workflow before you start, so the time saved is provable, not anecdotal.
  5. Then scale. Once one workflow holds for a week, copy the same backbone to the next use case. Pilot → Measure → Scale.

Why it cuts collection time

  • Day 1–2: map fields, create form and define folder structure.
  • Day 3–5: build tracker, reminders and exception views.
  • Day 6–7: pilot, measure follow-ups removed and freeze SOP.
PILOT TARGET 7 days to a working pilot workflow
PilotMeasureScale
CONTROL POINT

Measure baseline follow-ups, pilot one client group, refine the SOP, then scale to the firm.
